rows.why_long: Underdog higher 2.5 needs 56% per pick for your entry; fair view 66% (draftkings 4.5, moved to this line). Averaging 3.2 over the last 8 games, higher than 2.5 in 62% of them (raw 57%, shrunk 65%). Projects 3.2 (raw 56%, shrunk 65%).
why_points: The pick: Carries higher 2.5 on Underdog. Each pick has to win 56% of the time for a typical entry to make money; the sportsbooks' fair view (draftkings 4.5, moved to this line) is 66%.
Other apps: PrizePicks 4. This is the best number for the higher side.
Game log, most recent first: 3, 5, 0, 2, 1, 9, 4, 3. Weighted average 3.2; went higher than 2.5 in 5 of 8 games (62% recency-weighted).
Trending down: last 3 games average 2.7 vs 3.8 in the games before.
How much he swings: game to game he typically moves about ±2.4, so the line is 0.3 of those swings below his average (standard deviations) — a modest gap.
Projection: we expect 3.2 carries on average; in a typical game 2.5 (a few big games pull the average up, so the typical game is what we compare with the line) — 0.0 below the line.

Keeping it honest: on their own, recent games (form) say 57% and the matchup 56%. The sportsbooks are usually close to right, and these methods have only partly beaten them (weights measured on NFL week 2), so we pull them most of the way toward the market: form 65%, matchup 65%.
Bottom line: we give it 65% to win and it needs 56%. The edge is the difference: +8.9 points; that works out to about +16¢ per $1 bet over the long run.
Risks: low line - one play can decide it.
